instructions: Ambiguity hunt. Choose the answer labels, then argue the strongest case for one wrong option in case {label, text}. Set flag to one sentence when that case is defensible or a constraint is missing, else null.

items.stem: A company stores sensitive files in an Amazon S3 bucket that uses server-side encryption with a customer managed AWS KMS key (SSE-KMS). The key policy allows IAM policies in the account to control access to the key. A new application role has an IAM policy that allows s3:GetObject and s3:PutObject on the bucket and allows no KMS actions. The application only downloads existing objects from the bucket. Every request from the application fails with an access denied error. Which change will fix the problem with LEAST privilege?

options.label: A
options.text: Add a statement to the IAM policy of the role that allows kms:Decrypt on the ARN of the customer managed key that encrypts the bucket.

options.label: B
options.text: Add a statement to the IAM policy of the role that allows every KMS action, kms:*, on every KMS key in the account.

options.label: C
options.text: Add a statement to the IAM policy of the role that allows kms:GenerateDataKey on the ARN of the customer managed key that encrypts the bucket.

options.label: D
options.text: Replace the S3 statements in the IAM policy of the role with one statement that allows every Amazon S3 action, s3:*, on the bucket.

items.stem: A media company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances that creates large video files. Company policy requires that each file is encrypted at rest with a key that the security team controls in AWS KMS. The application must encrypt each file itself before it stores the file in Amazon S3. Later, other authorized applications must be able to decrypt each file. What should the application do for each file?

options.label: A
options.text: Call GenerateDataKey with the KMS key, encrypt the file locally with the plaintext data key, and store the plaintext data key with the encrypted file.

options.label: B
options.text: Call the Encrypt operation with the KMS key and the whole video file as the plaintext, and store the ciphertext that AWS KMS returns in Amazon S3.

options.label: C
options.text: Download the key material of the KMS key to the application, encrypt the file locally with that key material, and store the file in Amazon S3.

options.label: D
options.text: Call GenerateDataKey with the KMS key, encrypt the file locally with the plaintext data key, and store the encrypted data key with the encrypted file.

items.stem: A company stores customer orders in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The table uses the default encryption at rest, and no one has changed its encryption settings. A new security rule says that the security team must decide which IAM roles can use the encryption key of the table. The team must also audit each use of that key in AWS CloudTrail. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Switch the encryption of the table to the AWS managed key for DynamoDB, and edit the key policy of that key so that it names the allowed roles.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a customer managed KMS key with a key policy that names the allowed roles, and switch the encryption of the table to that new key.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a key in an AWS CloudHSM key store that the company operates, and switch the encryption of the table to that customer managed key.

options.label: D
options.text: Keep the AWS owned key that encrypts the table, and create an AWS CloudTrail trail that records each use of that key in the account.

items.stem: A company has two AWS accounts in an organization in AWS Organizations. Account A owns a customer managed AWS KMS key that encrypts files in an Amazon S3 bucket. An application in account B runs with an IAM role and must decrypt data that is encrypted under this key. The key policy names only principals in account A. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with LEAST privilege? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: In account B, add a statement to the IAM policy of the role that allows kms:Decrypt with the wildcard character as the resource, so every key matches.

options.label: B
options.text: In account B, add a statement to the IAM policy of the role that allows kms:Decrypt on the ARN of the customer managed key in account A.

options.label: C
options.text: In account A, add a statement to the key policy that allows kms:Decrypt for the ARN of the IAM role of the application in account B.

options.label: D
options.text: In account B, attach a service control policy (SCP) to the account that allows kms:Decrypt on the ARN of the key in account A.

options.label: E
options.text: In account A, re-encrypt the files under the AWS managed key for Amazon S3, and share that AWS managed key with account B.

items.stem: A company stores sensitive files in an Amazon S3 bucket that uses server-side encryption with a customer managed AWS KMS key (SSE-KMS). The key policy allows IAM policies in the account to control access to the key. A new application role has an IAM policy that allows s3:GetObject and s3:PutObject on the bucket and allows no KMS actions. The application only uploads new objects in single PUT requests. Every request from the application fails with an access denied error. Which change will fix the problem with LEAST privilege?

options.label: A
options.text: Replace the S3 statements in the IAM policy of the role with one statement that allows every Amazon S3 action, s3:*, on the bucket.

options.label: B
options.text: Add a statement to the IAM policy of the role that allows every KMS action, kms:*, on every KMS key in the account.

options.label: C
options.text: Add a statement to the IAM policy of the role that allows kms:Decrypt on the ARN of the customer managed key that encrypts the bucket.

options.label: D
options.text: Add a statement to the IAM policy of the role that allows kms:GenerateDataKey on the ARN of the customer managed key that encrypts the bucket.

items.stem: A financial services company is moving a Java application to AWS. Regulations require that the application's encryption keys are generated and stored in single-tenant hardware security modules (HSMs) under the company's exclusive control. The application calls its cryptographic library through the Java Cryptography Extension (JCE) interface, and the company does not want to change this code. The keys must stay available if one Availability Zone fails. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Create an AWS CloudHSM cluster with two HSMs in two Availability Zones, and generate and use the keys through the CloudHSM client libraries.

options.label: B
options.text: Create customer managed keys in AWS KMS in the default key store, and allow the application role to use the keys in each key policy.

options.label: C
options.text: Run HSM appliances that the company owns in two of its data centers, and connect them to the VPC through AWS Direct Connect.

options.label: D
options.text: Use the AWS managed keys that AWS KMS creates for each service, and limit their use by editing the key policy of each managed key.

items.stem: A security team created a customer managed AWS KMS key with a custom key policy. The key policy has one statement, which gives full access to the team's administrator role. Developer roles have IAM policies that allow kms:Decrypt on the ARN of the key, but their Decrypt calls fail with an access denied error. From now on, the team wants to centrally manage access to this key with IAM policies, as it does for other resources. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a KMS grant for each developer role that allows kms:Decrypt on the key, and create another grant for every new developer role.

options.label: B
options.text: Attach an IAM policy to the developer roles that allows every KMS action, kms:*, with the wildcard character as the resource of the statement.

options.label: C
options.text: Add a statement to the key policy that allows access for the account principal, so that IAM policies in the account can allow use of the key.

options.label: D
options.text: Attach the AdministratorAccess managed policy to the developer roles, so that the roles get full access to every resource in the account.

items.stem: A company stores many terabytes of objects in Amazon S3. The objects are encrypted with a symmetric customer managed AWS KMS key, and the security team wrote its own key policy for that key. A new company policy requires the company to rotate the key material every year. The security team must keep control of the key policy. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Run a scheduled AWS Lambda function every year that copies each object onto itself, so that Amazon S3 encrypts every object under new data keys.

options.label: B
options.text: Switch the encryption of the bucket to the AWS managed key for Amazon S3, because AWS rotates the key material of that key every year.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a new customer managed key every year, re-encrypt all objects in the bucket under the new key, and then schedule the old key for deletion.

options.label: D
options.text: Enable automatic key rotation on the customer managed key, and keep the existing key policy and the key ID that the applications already use.

items.stem: An application encrypts data on the client side with a single-Region AWS KMS key in us-east-1. The application replicates the encrypted data to us-west-2 for disaster recovery. During an outage in us-east-1, an application role in us-west-2 must decrypt the replicated data without a cross-Region call to us-east-1. The company accepts a one-time re-encryption of the existing data. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Write a key policy for the replica key in us-west-2 that allows the application role in us-west-2 to use the replica key for decryption.

options.label: B
options.text: Update the existing single-Region key in us-east-1 so that it becomes a multi-Region key, and create a replica of that key in us-west-2.

options.label: C
options.text: Allow the application role in us-west-2 to use kms:Decrypt on the ARN of the existing key in us-east-1, and call that ARN during the outage.

options.label: D
options.text: Create a new multi-Region primary key in us-east-1, create a replica of it in us-west-2, and encrypt the data under the primary key.

options.label: E
options.text: Create a single-Region key in us-west-2, and run a scheduled job that decrypts each replicated object and re-encrypts it under that key.

items.stem: A company encrypts the data of one customer with a dedicated customer managed AWS KMS key. The contract with that customer ends today. The company must stop every cryptographic use of the key as soon as possible. A legal review in 60 days can require the company to read the data again, so the company must make sure that access can be restored. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Disable the key now, and enable the key again later if the legal review requires the company to read the data of the customer.

options.label: B
options.text: Schedule the key for deletion with the longest waiting period, and cancel the deletion if the legal review requires access to the data.

options.label: C
options.text: Remove kms:Decrypt and kms:Encrypt from every IAM policy in the account that names the key, and keep the key policy as it is.

options.label: D
options.text: Add a statement to the key policy that denies all cryptographic operations to every principal, and remove that statement after the legal review.

items.stem: A company signs contracts with an asymmetric RSA key in AWS KMS. Customers verify the signatures with the public key of that KMS key. The applications that sign contracts refer to the key through an alias, not through its key ID. A new security policy requires the company to rotate the signing key. The applications must keep working without code changes. What should the company do?

options.label: A
options.text: Import new RSA key material into the existing asymmetric KMS key, and keep the alias that points to the existing KMS key.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a new asymmetric RSA KMS key for signing, and update the alias so that it points to the new KMS key instead of the old one.

options.label: C
options.text: Enable automatic key rotation on the existing asymmetric KMS key, and keep the alias that points to the existing KMS key.

options.label: D
options.text: Start an on-demand rotation of the existing asymmetric KMS key, and keep the alias that points to the existing KMS key.

items.stem: A financial services company is moving a Java application to AWS. Regulations require that the application's encryption keys are protected by hardware security modules (HSMs) validated at FIPS 140-3 Level 3. The application calls AWS KMS through the AWS SDK. The security team must write the key policy of each key and must not depend on keys that an AWS service controls. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Create an AWS CloudHSM cluster with two HSMs in two Availability Zones, and generate and use the keys through the CloudHSM client libraries.

options.label: B
options.text: Use the AWS managed keys that AWS KMS creates for each service, and limit their use by editing the key policy of each managed key.

options.label: C
options.text: Create customer managed keys in AWS KMS in the default key store, and allow the application role to use the keys in each key policy.

options.label: D
options.text: Run HSM appliances that the company owns in two of its data centers, and connect them to the VPC through AWS Direct Connect.
